title: Office 2013 becomes available
impact: Click-to-Run installs become common; with them, other apps cannot see the ACE provider that Office installs, so .NET apps that read Excel or Access files through ACE break on those PCs

title: Office 2013 becomes available with extended support scheduled to end in April 2023
impact: PCs moved to Office 2013 have a known end date, so the next Office upgrade and retesting of Excel and Access integrations can be planned

title: Extended support for SQL Server 2000 ends
impact: Databases still on SQL Server 2000 get no more security updates, and moving them means checking old syntax such as *= outer joins

title: Microsoft says Windows 8 stays supported only for two years after Windows 8.1 ships, so PCs must move to 8.1 by January 2016
impact: PCs left on Windows 8 lose support in 2016, so client apps have to be tested on Windows 8.1

title: Support for .NET Framework 1.1 SP1 ends (except as part of Windows Server 2003)
impact: Apps still on the 1.1 runtime get no more fixes and need to be moved to a later framework

title: Extended support for Visual Studio .NET 2003 ends
impact: The Visual Studio .NET 2003 IDE gets no more fixes, so teams still building with it are on an unsupported toolchain unless they upgrade

title: .NET Framework 4.5.1 ships with Visual Studio 2013 and Windows 8.1
impact: It replaces 4.5 in place, so apps on 4.5 machines run on 4.5.1 after update without being rebuilt

title: Visual Studio 2013 ships
impact: Ships with .NET Framework 4.5.1; the solution file starts to record the exact IDE version, which shows up as noise in version control when people use different versions

title: Visual Studio 2013 ships with extended support scheduled to end in April 2024
impact: Teams building with Visual Studio 2013 have a known end date for the IDE, so the next IDE upgrade can be planned
